concepts.heading: Understanding Love Addiction & Codependency
concepts.plain: Sometimes a relationship turns into something you feel driven to do, not something you choose.

concepts.heading: What Is Love Addiction?
concepts.plain: Love addiction is being fixated on someone and mistaking intensity for closeness.

concepts.heading: Codependency: The Other Side
concepts.plain: Codependency is looking after others so much that you forget your own needs.

concepts.heading: The Love Addict/Love Avoidant Dance
concepts.plain: One person chases and the other pulls away, round and round.

checks.explanation: Intimacy. Love addiction involves obsessive focus on a romantic interest and confusing intensity with intimacy.

options: Excessive caretaking at the expense of your own needs
checks.explanation: Excessive caretaking at the expense of your own needs. Codependency involves excessive caretaking at the expense of your own needs, along with poor boundaries.

e56bc4e9-0633-405f-b914-dc2f17c5ca55.takeaway: Needing a relationship to feel okay, or losing yourself in caring for someone, are patterns you can change.

concepts.heading: Recognizing Compulsive Patterns
concepts.plain: These patterns can feel normal because they are all you have known.

concepts.heading: The Neurochemistry of Love Addiction
concepts.plain: Falling in love floods your brain with powerful chemicals.

concepts.heading: Red Flags: Compulsive Relationship Patterns
concepts.plain: Warning signs include jumping straight from one relationship into the next.

concepts.heading: Distinguishing Healthy Desire from Compulsion
concepts.plain: Not every strong feeling is a problem. The lesson shows how to tell the difference.

concepts.heading: Self-Assessment Questions
concepts.plain: Ask yourself honestly: do I only feel complete when I am in a relationship?

checks.prompt: Falling in love triggers a neurochemical cocktail similar to…
checks.explanation: Cocaine. Falling in love triggers a neurochemical cocktail similar to cocaine, including dopamine for reward and craving.

checks.prompt: Which is a red flag for compulsive patterns?
options: Jumping from relationship to relationship without processing
checks.explanation: Jumping from relationship to relationship without processing. Serial monogamy, jumping from relationship to relationship without processing the previous one, is a red flag.

4ee2084f-fa6c-4081-a32c-91fab164ceb5.takeaway: Strong feelings are not the problem. The warning sign is feeling you cannot be okay alone.

concepts.heading: Love Bombing, Trauma Bonds & Toxic Cycles
concepts.plain: Knowing how manipulation works helps you get free of it.

concepts.heading: Love Bombing
concepts.plain: Love bombing is flooding someone with attention and gifts in order to control them.

concepts.heading: Trauma Bonds
concepts.plain: A trauma bond forms when someone hurts you, then is loving, over and over.

concepts.heading: Breaking the Cycle
concepts.plain: Breaking free takes several steps. You do not have to do it alone.

concepts.heading: Recognizing Toxic Patterns in Yourself
concepts.plain: Look honestly at your own behaviour too.

options: Excessive attention and gifts used to manipulate someone
checks.explanation: Excessive attention and gifts used to manipulate someone. Love bombing is the deliberate use of excessive attention, affection, and gifts to manipulate someone into a relationship.

options: Intermittent reinforcement: cycles of abuse and affection
checks.explanation: Intermittent reinforcement: cycles of abuse and affection. Trauma bonds form through intermittent reinforcement — cycles of abuse and affection that create powerful neurological attachments.

cda693e9-7f0c-49c1-a193-bc52361970c4.takeaway: Too much, too fast can be a tactic. Hot-and-cold treatment creates a bond that is hard to leave.

concepts.heading: Recovery & Building Healthy Habits
concepts.plain: You can break these patterns. It takes commitment and support.

concepts.heading: The Stages of Recovery
concepts.plain: It happens in stages. The first is seeing that the pattern is a problem.

concepts.heading: Practical Recovery Tools
concepts.plain: After leaving a toxic relationship, at least 90 days of no contact helps your brain reset.

concepts.heading: The Healthy Relationship Checklist
concepts.plain: Healthy means you add to each other's lives without being each other's whole life.

concepts.heading: Building Secure Attachment
concepts.plain: Secure attachment can be earned through steady, reliable behaviour.

concepts.heading: When You're Ready to Date Again
concepts.plain: When you date again, go slowly.

checks.prompt: What is the 90-day no-contact rule for?
options: Letting your neurochemistry reset after a toxic relationship
checks.explanation: Letting your neurochemistry reset after a toxic relationship. After leaving a toxic relationship, at least 90 days of no contact gives your neurochemistry time to reset.

checks.after: When You're Ready to Date Again
checks.prompt: What is the advice for dating again?
checks.explanation: Slow is the new fast. Slow is the new fast.

b0427e1d-46cf-4338-90f8-a2d99573b4ae.takeaway: Recovery is possible. Notice the pattern, take time apart, build your own life, and go slowly.
